comparator.name: Tax Law
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 guide: revised curriculum introduced from September 2025; later-year cohort continuation unresolved
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official BA-FIS guide explicitly separates revised years 1 and 2 from the outgoing third year. The supported revised years contain twelve required 5-EC courses each, totaling 60 + 60 = 120 EC. The displayed third year is explicitly for entrants in 2024 or earlier; its 40-EC required group, 15-EC elective space and 5-EC thesis are historical cohort context and are excluded from these components. The guide says the revised third year will appear in the 2027–2028 edition. Published first/second-year requirements therefore establish partial revised-cohort coverage, not a verified complete pathway for a Fall 2026 entrant or a guaranteed 2027–2028/2028–2029 sequence. Zero-credit language test and tutoring/Leiden Law Practices formation add no credits. Current full-time/part-time pacing must be checked against the applicable regulations before reconstruction is completed. External sources checked 2026-10-08; no independent UCR fit assessment was performed.

exception.reason: A reliable complete current Tax Law pathway cannot yet be established. The 2026–2027 guide publishes revised first- and second-year requirements but reserves the displayed third year for students who entered in 2024 or earlier. Combining these cohorts would count outgoing requirements as new-cohort progression. The university says the revised third year will be published in the 2027–2028 guide. Retain the supported 120 EC and defer full curriculum reconstruction; do not infer the remaining course requirements from the 180-EC degree size.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported revised curriculum consists of 60 EC of first-year legal foundations and 60 EC of second-year legal and fiscal study, including income taxation, indirect taxation, financial accounting, public-sector economics and tax ethics. All 24 credited units are 5 EC. Third-year course requirements and any future elective/thesis allocation for the revised cohort remain unresolved. Outgoing 40 + 15 + 5 EC are historical context, not components of the revised reconstruction.
